ci_method: Callaway-Sant'Anna (2021) group-time ATTs aggregated with the 'simple' weighting (each ATT(g,t) weighted by its number of treated county-years), never-treated counties as the comparison group, universal base period; SE = 0.2104 from the multiplier bootstrap clustered at the county level (5,000 iterations, did::att_gt bstrap=TRUE, clustervars=county_id); CI = estimate +/- 1.96*SE. This interval reflects sampling uncertainty only and does NOT include uncertainty about the parallel-trends assumption, which is untestable for the cohort carrying 69% of the weight (see assumptions_checked).

Callaway & Sant'Anna (2021) doubly-robust group-time ATT(g,t) with never-treated counties as the comparison group, aggregated with weights proportional to the number of treated county-years per cohort (the 'simple' aggregation, which exactly reproduces the requested treated-county-year-weighted ATT; verified by hand, weights sum to all 3,185 treated county-years). 95% CI = point estimate +/- 1.96 * SE, where the SE (0.210) comes from the multiplier bootstrap clustered at the county level, 2,000 replications, seed 20261027.

Callaway-Sant'Anna (2021) doubly-robust group-time ATTs aggregated with weights proportional to the number of treated county-years in each (cohort, year) cell (the 'simple' aggregation, which is exactly the ATT across treated county-years); 95% CI from the multiplier bootstrap clustered at the county level (5,000 draws), SE = 0.217. Corroborated by a nonparametric county-level bootstrap (400 reps, SE = 0.209, percentile CI [6.74, 7.63]), by CS analytic influence-function SEs (CI [6.77, 7.59]), and by Sun-Abraham/fixest with county-clustered SEs (7.179, CI [6.81, 7.55]).

Anderson-Rubin weak-instrument-robust 95% confidence set, obtained by inverting the heteroskedasticity-robust (HC1) AR test over a grid of candidate betas from -500 to 500 in steps of 0.001 and comparing to the chi2(1) 95% critical value (3.8415). The resulting set is contiguous and bounded: [-0.051, 1.804]. Cross-checked three ways: (a) independently re-estimated in R (identical set, [-0.050, 1.800] on a 0.005 grid); (b) closed-form algebraic inversion of the homoskedastic AR quadratic, giving [-0.008, 1.643]; (c) AR using the F(1, n-4) rather than chi2(1) critical value, giving [-0.051, 1.829]. AR is used instead of the conventional 2SLS Wald interval because the instrument is weak (first-stage robust F = 4.22), which makes the Wald interval's 95% coverage invalid; AR retains correct coverage for any instrument strength and is the optimal weak-IV-robust test in a just-identified model. For reference, the naive 2SLS Wald interval would be [0.018, 0.408] and the tF-adjusted (Lee, McCrary, Moreira & Porter 2022) interval is [-0.897, 1.323]; both the AR and tF intervals contain zero.

Anderson-Rubin 95% weak-instrument-robust confidence set (HC1), computed by grid inversion over beta in [-60, 60] at 0.0002-0.05 resolution; the set is a single bounded interval. Reported instead of the conventional 2SLS Wald interval because the first stage is weak (robust F = 4.22 < 10), which invalidates normal-approximation inference. For reference, the naive 2SLS HC1 Wald interval is [0.018, 0.408] and the homoskedastic AR interval is [-0.008, 1.643].

Anderson-Rubin weak-instrument-robust 95% CI, obtained by inverting the heteroskedasticity-robust (HC1) AR test for H0: beta = b0 over a grid of b0 and solving AR p-value = 0.05 by root-finding. The homoskedastic AR CI is [-0.008, 1.643]; both contain zero. The conventional 2SLS Wald CI is [0.018, 0.408] (HC1) / [0.015, 0.411] (homoskedastic), but it is NOT reported as the headline interval because with a first-stage F of 4.4 the 2SLS t-test is severely size-distorted (Lee et al. 2022 require F > 104.7 for a nominal 5% t-test; Stock-Yogo require F > 16.38 for 5% maximal relative bias). The 2000-replication nonparametric bootstrap percentile interval [-0.079, 0.690] also contains zero and is likewise not valid under weak identification.

Visit-level linear-probability DiD (hit ~ program*post), cluster-robust (CR0) standard errors clustered on practice_id (60 clusters), normal 95% interval; SE = 0.97 pp. Corroborated by wild cluster bootstrap-t with Rademacher weights, 2000 reps, null imposed ([5.90, 9.90] pp, p<0.0005) and by practice-level Welch t-test on the 60 practice-specific pre/post changes ([5.90, 9.82] pp). Randomization inference permuting the program label across the 60 practices (2000 draws) gives p<0.0005 with a null 2.5-97.5 percentile range of [-2.84, 2.81] pp.

Wild cluster bootstrap (Rademacher weights, 4999 reps, imposing the null, clustered on the 60 practices) around the visit-level 2x2 DiD OLS; 95% interval. Agrees with CR1 cluster-robust SEs using t(59) critical values [6.09, 10.03], with clustering on member [5.93, 10.19], with the practice-period collapsed WLS DiD [5.40, 10.73], and with a practice-level Welch t-test on the 60 pre-to-post changes [6.01, 9.99]. Randomization inference (5000 permutations of the program label across the 60 practices) gives p < 0.0002.

Visit-level OLS (linear probability model) of 14-day follow-up on program x post, SEs clustered at the practice level (CR1, 60 clusters), 95% interval from t(59). Confirmed by wild cluster bootstrap-t with Rademacher weights, B=2000 (95% percentile-t CI [5.91, 9.79], p=0.0005) and by randomization inference permuting program status across the 60 practices (B=2000, p=0.0005, null sd 1.42pp).

OLS of outcome on treatment with all 12 pre-specified baseline covariates (Lin 2013 interacted/centered specification), HC2 heteroskedasticity-robust 95% CI. Unadjusted difference-in-means (0.134, [0.058, 0.211]), Welch t-interval, nonparametric bootstrap percentile (5,000 reps, [0.056, 0.212]) and AIPW causal-forest (0.133, [0.064, 0.202]) all agree to within 0.002.

OLS of outcome on treatment plus all 12 pre-treatment covariates (continuous terms linear, region/education/employment as factors), HC2 heteroskedasticity-robust SEs, 95% t-interval. Pre-specified as primary. Agrees with: unadjusted Welch diff-in-means 0.134 [0.058,0.211]; Lin (2013) fully-interacted centered-covariate estimator 0.132 [0.064,0.201]; nonparametric bootstrap (2,000 reps) [0.059,0.204]; causal-forest AIPW 0.133 [0.064,0.202]; randomization-inference p=0.0006.

OLS with Lin (2013) covariate adjustment (all 12 baseline covariates, mean-centered, fully interacted with treatment), HC2 heteroskedasticity-robust SEs, t-distribution 95% CI. Agrees closely with the unadjusted difference in means (0.134, HC2 CI [0.058, 0.211]), a nonparametric bootstrap (10,000 reps: [0.057, 0.211]), and an AIPW causal-forest ATE (0.134, SE 0.035); randomization-inference p = 0.0006.
